title: Numeric input validation fails
description:
This example code using the `sv_numeric` rule function, which I copied from the package help pages (https://rstudio.github.io/shinyvalidate/reference/sv_numeric.html), fails for me: ``` library(shiny) library(shinyvalidate) ui <- fluidPage( textInput("rating", "Rating") ) server <- function(input, output, session) { iv <- InputValidator$new() iv$add_rule("rating", sv_numeric()) iv$enable() } shinyApp(ui, server) ``` When I run the app and enter a valid number, e.g. the number 1, the validator does not remove the "A number is required" error message. I checked a few other numeric rule functions and they all had problems too. If I reuse the above code but swap in `sv_integer()`, then within the app an error message is immediately displayed saying "An unexpected error occurred during input validation: non-numeric argument to binary operator". This is before I've even tried to type anything. Additionally, a warning is displayed in the console: ``` Warning: Error in %%: non-numeric argument to binary operator 74: withCallingHandlers 73: suppressWarnings 72: rule_fn 71: 69: rule$rule 55: 54: mapply 53: self$`_validate_impl` 52: self$validate 51: :: shiny observe 50: 3: runApp 2: print.shiny.appobj 1: ``` If I again reuse the above code but swap in `sv_between(0, 100)`, then the validator accepts some numbers but not others in the range. E.g., I found that 0, 1, 10, and 100 are all considered valid, but 5 is considered invalid. I also checked some non-numeric rule functions, specifically `sv_email` and `sv_in_set`, and both seemed to work fine in my limited testing. So the package isn't totally broken on my computer, and the issue seems to be limited to the numeric rule functions. Here's my session info:

title: `freezeReactiveValue()` causes `An unexpected error occurred during input validation` with `iv$add_rule()` and `updateSelectInput()`
description:
The error is caused by:

1. adding `selected = character()` to `updateSelectInput()`
2. using `choices = = character()` in `updateSelectInput()`

```
ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset", c("pressure", "cars")),
  selectInput("column", "Choose column", character(0)),
  verbatimTextOutput("summary")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  dataset <- reactive(get(input$dataset, "package:datasets"))
  
  observeEvent(input$dataset, {
    freezeReactiveValue(input, "column")
    updateSelectInput(inputId = "column", choices = names(dataset()),
                      selected = character())
  })
  
  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    summary(dataset()[[input$column]])
  })
  
  iv <- InputValidator$new()
  iv$add_rule("column", sv_optional())
  iv$enable()
  
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Add 'remove_rule' method to InputValidator?
description:
I haven't found an easy way to create a conditional `sv_required` rule, and there doesn't appear to be a method for removing / clearing an existing rule that was added by `add_rule`.

In my app I have a set of inputs that are linked. If some values are chosen in the parent input, there are no options in the child input, so my thinking was that I would have a rule of the input being required when there are options in the child input, but drop that rule when there are no options. So basically, if the user has some choices in the `selectInput`, they need to pick one of those options, otherwise there's no need to have a rule on that input as they have nothing to select from.

I don't think the `test` argument of `sv_required` is sufficient because I think that only allows tests on the input being validated? In my case I am doing a check on multiple inputs, not just the input I'm applying the validation to, so e.g. I am testing if input a meets condition 1 and input b meets condition 2, then apply validation rule to input b.

title: Allow for partial enable/disable of validator trees
description:
Currently, if you add a leaf validator to a root validator, the leaf validator enable() method is disregarded, and you can either enable or disable the tree as a whole by calling enable on the root validator. 

However there are cases, such as dynamic UIs, where you would like to disable only the leaf validator because it targets a control that is not rendered in those circumstances, all while still validating the rest of the validation tree.

title: Feature request: dateInput validation
description:
I'm guessing there is already a way within the current shinyvalidate infrastructure (I'm new to using the package) for doing this, but it'd be nice if there was a baked-in sv_date() function for validating whether users have provided a valid date (using a specific format) to a dateInput. 

The reason this is useful, among other reasons, is that users don't have to use the date picker with this input. Instead, they can use the backspace/delete keys to empty the input box and then type a date manually. Except they can also type gibberish to a large extent, in my experience! Shiny attempts to coerce what is entered to a date, but this can lead to nonsensical inputs...

title: `sv_numeric()` produces unexpected validation error message
description:
**Context:** Using `add_rule(..., sv_numeric()))` with `numericInput()`.
**User interaction:** Enter non-numeric value, e.g., some combination of `- , e .`
**Issue:** The message shown to the user is not the one set in `message` and cannot be configured. 

**Example app:**

``` r
library(shiny)  # version 1.7.1
library(shinyvalidate)   # version 0.1.2

ui <- fluidPage(
  numericInput("number", "Number", value = 0),
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  iv <- InputValidator$new()
  iv$add_rule("number", sv_numeric(message = "A number is required."))
  iv$enable()
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

<sup>Created on 2022-07-15 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1)</sup>


**Expected shinyvalidate output:**  `A number is required`
**Actual shinyvalidate output:** `Must not contain `NA` values`

The error message should be the one set by the user, or the NA-specific error message should be configurable, because

- For apps developed in other languages an English error message sticks out.
- For non-technical users this error messsage may not be helpful.

------

I believe the message is created by `sv_basic()` here: https://github.com/rstudio/shinyvalidate/blob/575f5865fcb028656b58760ba357b6247b97d866/R/rules.R#L1417

`sv_numeric()` composes a rule, starting with `sv_basic()` and adds the numeric-specific rules on top of it:https://github.com/rstudio/shinyvalidate/blob/575f5865fcb028656b58760ba357b6247b97d866/R/rules.R#L500

The basic rules are checked first and validations of the basic rules are triggered first. This includes the "no NA" validation check. The corresponding error message is hard coded 
https://github.com/rstudio/shinyvalidate/blob/575f5865fcb028656b58760ba357b6247b97d866/R/rules.R#L1448.

title: Don't check validation of an input if it is hidden with a `conditionalPanel()`
description:
I'd like to have an option not to check validation if an input is hidden with a `conditionalPanel()`. I'd like to require answers to all of my items. However, using branching logic, I hide some items based on participants' responses with a `conditionalPanel()`, and I would not like their validation to be checked on the items that are hidden. Consider the following example:

```
1. What is your favorite sport? (radio button input)

a. baseball
b. basketball
c. football
d. soccer
e. other (please specify)

2. You selected "other"--please specify: (textbox input)
```

Let's say I show Item 2 conditionally only when "other" (option `e`) is selected for Item 1. I want both items to be required, but only if the item is shown to participants. I don't want validation to be checked for Item 2 unless it is shown.

The reason why this would be helpful is that I'd like to allow participants to proceed to the next survey only after they have completed all (shown) items. However, `iv$is_valid()` evaluates as `FALSE` because some of the "required" items are hidden based on their responses and they do not have an opportunity to complete them.

title: Allow for validators not related to an input
description:
I have an app where the UI is revealed only as the user completes the prior UI section. 

I'm using shinyvalidate to validate my inputs and it's GREAT. But some of my validation isn't entirely tied to inputs, and I'd love to just check a child validators for my state.

This comes up in 2 ways:
1) I am using reactables as inputs, so they don't have a formal representation in `input`. 
2) I don't want the validator to populate until an API call has returned, not when the input is selected.

# App Architecture Sketch
I've tried to put together a simplified sketch/pseudocode of my use case below. I've left out a bunch of the more "on-label" use of shinyvalidate here, because that's clear. But unlike in the example below, my real app is more like 5 "normal" shinyvalidate cases and 2 unrelated to an input.

## ui
```
div(
  textInput("text1"), 
  tab_start_hidden(
    id = "table_ui",
    reactableOutput("table"), 
    textInput("text2")
  ), 
  hidden_ui(
    id = "submit_ui",
    actionButton("submit")
  )
)
```

## server
```
{
   iv <- shinyvalidate::InputValidator$new()
   iv$add_rule("text1", sv_required())
   iv$add_rule("text2", sv_required())
   iv$enable()

  table_data <- eventReactive(input$text1, doApiCall(input$text1))

  # Would love to just be able to check a validator here
  observeEvent(table_data, if (table_data is not null) unhide("table_ui"))

  output$table <- renderReactable(table_data)

  selected <- get_reactable_row_selected("table")

  # Would love to check child validator
  observeEvent({selected, iv$is_valid()}, if (!is.null(selected()) & iv$is_valid()) unhide("submit_ui")
}
```

title: Errors thrown from validation rules are hidden from user
description:
Currently, a rule that throws results in the input passing validation (at least that's what it looks like to me on cursory investigation). In the below example, the text input has no visual indicator that anything is wrong, and `iv$is_valid()` returns `TRUE`.

An error in validation should probably manifest as a validation failure. We need to decide what kind of message to display:

1. "An unexpected error occurred while processing this input"
2. Actually display the message (though when Shiny [error sanitization](https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/sanitize-errors.html) is enabled, we'd need to fall back to a generic message like option 1 for most errors)

```r
library(shiny)
library(shinyvalidate)

ui <- fluidPage(
  textInput("input1", NULL),
  p(
    "Validation passing: ",
    textOutput("validation_result", container = tags$strong)
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  iv <- InputValidator$new()
  iv$add_rule("input1", ~ stop("boom"))
  iv$enable()
  
  output$validation_result <- renderText({
    if (iv$is_valid()) "yes" else "no"
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

title: Add a validator function that checks for set membership
description:
A validator function that checks a field for inclusion in a specified set should be added (as `sv_in_set()`). It should probably have the following form:

```
sv_in_set(
  set,
  allow_nan = FALSE,
  message = NULL,
  msg_limit = 3
)
```

We don't need the `allow_na` arg that's in other validator functions since we can include an `NA` in the `set` vector. The `msg_limit` option will impose a limit of `set` values to include in the automatically-generated error message (i.e., when `message = NULL`). So, if the number of elements provided in `set` is greater than `msg_limit` then only the first `<msg_limit>` set elements will be echoed along with text that states how many extra elements are part of the `set`.

title: Revisit child validators
description:
Currently, validators (parents) can add other validators (children). When a validator becomes a child, it loses its own sense of enable/disable; instead, it is implicitly disabled, and the responsibility for showing feedback is essentially bequeathed to its parent.

[This article](https://uxmovement.com/forms/why-users-make-more-errors-with-instant-inline-validation/) argues for deferred validation for most fields, _with exceptions made_ for difficult-to-get-right fields like passwords with onerous requirements, or usernames that have to pass a uniqueness check.

Currently this would only be possible by creating completely separate, unrelated validators, one for deferred validation and one for eager validation. That would work, but it means that the burden of bringing the validators together for `is_valid()` purposes falls on whomever needs to consume the form input, and that feels suboptimal.

Giving child validators their own enable state is the obvious fix (maybe a trinary state: enabled, disabled, and NA for "inherit"). But the problem with this is that child validators can be added with conditions, conditions that only the parent knows about. We would need to change this so that conditions aren't added to the parent-child relationship, but to the child itself.

Instead of:

```r
child_iv <- produce_child_validator_somehow()

iv <- InputValidator$new()
iv$add_validator(child_iv, when = ~ input$mode == "upload")
```

it would become:

```r
child_iv <- produce_child_validator_somehow()
child_iv$set_condition(~ input$mode == "upload")

iv <- InputValidator$new()
iv$add_validator(child_iv)
```

That seems pretty reasonable, actually.
